pages.text: Split a reaction in two and make its electrons go round by a wire, and its free energy comes out as a voltage: $(thing)ΔG = −nFE$(). The Nernst equation says how the voltage moves with the reactants: $(thing)E = E° − (RT/nF)·ln Q$().

The $(item)Fuel Cell$() burns Hydrogen (or Ammonia) with Oxygen as a current. Drawing more current costs voltage - so the power, V·i, peaks part-way, near 1 A/cm². Too little current and it floods; too much and it starves.

The $(item)Vanadium Flow Battery$() stores 50 million FE in two tanks of vanadium electrolyte. Its voltage follows its charge, and right-clicking it reads both; it stops taking charge at 95%. Salt water through the Electrolytic Cell gives $(fluid)Chlorine$() and $(item)Caustic Soda$(); lithium carbonate gives back lithium.
